newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Foreigners dominate Swiss mutual fund scene - survey.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners dominate Swiss mutual fund scene - survey.

text.p: Foreign investors make up the bulk of the clients of Swiss mutual funds and are pouring in an average 20 percent into the industry in fresh cash each year, a survey by Swiss asset management firm Swissca said.
The survey found that only one out of 10 Swiss investors had money in mutual funds compared to 18 percent in Europe.
Two-thirds of the Swiss surveyed did not even know what a mutual fund was.

"The majority of our clients are foreigners. Potential Swiss clients have yet to be sufficiently exploited," said Swissca's director general Serge Courtet, presenting the results of the survey at a Geneva asset management seminar.
Assets of Switzerland's mutual funds jumped by nearly $7 billion in January, according to Swiss mutual fund statistician Bopp ISB.
The survey said combined assets of public mutual funds set up by Swiss banks at home and abroad grew to 242.3 billion Swiss Francs at the end of January from 232.4 billion at end-1996.
Assets in the industry grew by 26 percent in 1996 with an average monthly net flow of 1.5 billion Swiss francs, according to Bopp ISB.
Courtet said Switzerland ranked third in the world in terms of mutual fund assets after France and Germany.

The bulk of the mutual fund assets of Swiss institutions were being managed in Luxembourg, worth 154 billion Swiss francs at end-1996, followed by Switzerland with 72 billion Swiss francs and some six billion francs in other centres.
The survey put the number of mutual funds managed by Swiss institutions at 1,316 as of end-1996, of which more than two-thirds were based in Luxembourg, up from some 450 in 1995.

Swiss Bank Corp controlled some 30 percent of the market with a share worth 69.2 billion Swiss francs in assets, followed by Union Bank of Switzerland with a 26 percent share worth 60.1 billion Swiss francs.
Courtet said nobody knew the total volume of assets of inhouse mutual funds managed by secretive private banks in Switzerland and that the total was likely to be worth millions of Swiss francs more.
Data on the total volume of assets managed is not published in Switzerland, a by-product of its culture of bank secrecy, and bank annual reports provide only scanty information.
"Nobody would give you such figures. Swiss private banks are very private. Swiss private bankers are happy when their banks' names do not appear in newspapers," Courtet said.
Total private wealth under management in Switzerland is more than $1.8 trillion, according to a recent survey by Credit Suisse First Boston Bank.
